nodes.name: Problem Constitution
nodes.capability: Constitutes a resolvable problem by integrating the relevant present condition, valued destination, and governing boundary.
nodes.accepts: An experienced concern, discrepancy, opportunity, or question.
nodes.produces: A bounded problem whose current state, success conditions, and admissible scope are explicit.
nodes.boundary: Defines what is to be resolved without explaining causes or selecting interventions.
nodes.excludes: Causal diagnosis, option design, commitment, execution, and feedback control.

nodes.name: Situation Characterization
nodes.capability: Forms a relevant account of the conditions from which resolution must begin.
nodes.accepts: Observations, claims, context, and unresolved discrepancies.
nodes.produces: A differentiated representation of the pertinent present situation.
nodes.boundary: Characterizes what currently obtains and what remains unknown.
nodes.excludes: Desired outcomes, causal explanations, and intervention proposals.

nodes.name: Outcome Valuation
nodes.capability: Determines what improvement means and how satisfactory resolution can be recognized.
nodes.accepts: Needs, purposes, preferences, obligations, and candidate outcome properties.
nodes.produces: Prioritized success criteria and tolerable residual conditions.
nodes.boundary: Defines valued ends and evaluation standards.
nodes.excludes: Present-state description, causal modeling, and choice among interventions.

nodes.name: Boundary Constitution
nodes.capability: Determines which conditions, interests, resources, and effects belong inside the problem.
nodes.accepts: Context, affected interests, dependencies, constraints, and available agency.
nodes.produces: An explicit scope with relevant inclusions, exclusions, and non-negotiable limits.
nodes.boundary: Sets the resolution envelope within which other capabilities operate.
nodes.excludes: Diagnosing mechanisms or deciding what action to take.

nodes.name: Explanatory Understanding
nodes.capability: Builds a warranted account of why the problem persists and where change can propagate.
nodes.accepts: A constituted problem plus observations, records, hypotheses, and uncertainty.
nodes.produces: An evidence-calibrated model of mechanisms, dependencies, and leverage.
nodes.boundary: Explains the situation sufficiently to inform intervention design.
nodes.excludes: Generating, choosing, or enacting a resolution.

nodes.name: Evidence Appraisal
nodes.capability: Establishes what information deserves reliance and with what confidence.
nodes.accepts: Observations, testimony, measurements, records, and competing claims.
nodes.produces: A weighted evidence base with gaps, conflicts, and confidence made explicit.
nodes.boundary: Assesses informational warrant rather than constructing the full explanation.
nodes.excludes: Value judgments and intervention selection.

nodes.name: Mechanism Modeling
nodes.capability: Represents the relationships through which conditions generate, sustain, or alter outcomes.
nodes.accepts: A bounded situation and appraised evidence.
nodes.produces: A causal or functional model identifying dependencies and potential leverage.
nodes.boundary: Models change-bearing relationships whether physical, social, logical, or informational.
nodes.excludes: Judging desired outcomes or committing to an intervention.

nodes.name: Uncertainty Representation
nodes.capability: Represents material unknowns, variability, ambiguity, and model limitations.
nodes.accepts: Evidence, mechanism models, disputed interpretations, and possible future conditions.
nodes.produces: A calibrated uncertainty structure showing what is unknown and why it matters.
nodes.boundary: Preserves uncertainty for later design and judgment instead of forcing false certainty.
nodes.excludes: Resolving value conflicts or selecting a course of action.

nodes.name: Resolution Synthesis
nodes.capability: Constructs coherent candidate ways to move the constituted situation toward valued outcomes.
nodes.accepts: A constituted problem, explanatory model, uncertainties, and available means.
nodes.produces: Distinct, internally coherent intervention candidates with anticipated effects.
nodes.boundary: Creates and develops possibilities without finally adopting one.
nodes.excludes: Final commitment, authorization, and enactment.

nodes.name: Intervention Generation
nodes.capability: Generates materially distinct mechanisms for changing the problem situation.
nodes.accepts: Leverage points, success criteria, boundary conditions, and available capabilities.
nodes.produces: A varied set of candidate interventions rather than superficial variants.
nodes.boundary: Expands the feasible possibility space.
nodes.excludes: Final comparison, adoption, and implementation.

nodes.name: Consequence Anticipation
nodes.capability: Projects intended, indirect, delayed, and failure consequences of candidate interventions.
nodes.accepts: Candidate interventions, mechanism models, affected interests, and uncertainty.
nodes.produces: Conditional consequence profiles across relevant criteria and contexts.
nodes.boundary: Examines what candidates may produce without deciding which should prevail.
nodes.excludes: Commitment and real-world execution.

nodes.name: Configuration Integration
nodes.capability: Combines compatible intervention elements into resolutions whose parts support rather than undermine one another.
nodes.accepts: Candidate mechanisms, consequence profiles, constraints, and dependencies.
nodes.produces: Coherent candidate configurations with internal conflicts exposed or resolved.
nodes.boundary: Ensures candidate-level systemic fit before selection.
nodes.excludes: Choosing or authorizing a configuration.

nodes.name: Resolution Commitment
nodes.capability: Converts evaluated possibilities into a defensible adopted course under tradeoffs and uncertainty.
nodes.accepts: Coherent candidates, consequence profiles, success criteria, uncertainty, and decision authority.
nodes.produces: An adopted resolution with rationale, accepted risks, and commitment conditions.
nodes.boundary: Determines which course will govern action.
nodes.excludes: Generating the option space or carrying the decision into effect.

nodes.name: Comparative Judgment
nodes.capability: Evaluates candidates across plural success criteria and unavoidable tradeoffs.
nodes.accepts: Candidate configurations, consequence profiles, and prioritized criteria.
nodes.produces: A transparent comparative assessment including dominated and non-comparable alternatives.
nodes.boundary: Structures preference among candidates without itself establishing adoption.
nodes.excludes: Option generation, authorization, and execution.

nodes.name: Robustness Judgment
nodes.capability: Tests whether a candidate remains acceptable across uncertainty, disruption, and plausible error.
nodes.accepts: Candidate resolutions, uncertainty structure, failure modes, and reversibility information.
nodes.produces: Risk exposure, robustness conditions, safeguards, and residual uncertainty.
nodes.boundary: Assesses resilience of choice rather than operational progress.
nodes.excludes: Ongoing feedback control after enactment.

nodes.name: Adoption Formation
nodes.capability: Establishes the authority, ownership, and willingness required for a resolution to govern action.
nodes.accepts: Comparative assessments, risk judgments, affected commitments, and decision rights.
nodes.produces: A selected and owned resolution with explicit conditions for reconsideration.
nodes.boundary: Closes deliberation provisionally and creates actionable commitment.
nodes.excludes: Mobilizing resources or performing the intervention.

nodes.name: Resolution Realization
nodes.capability: Translates an adopted resolution into coordinated changes in the world.
nodes.accepts: An adopted resolution, available agency, resources, and operational conditions.
nodes.produces: Enacted changes corresponding to the resolution's intended mechanism.
nodes.boundary: Makes the resolution real while preserving its governing intent.
nodes.excludes: Defining success, explaining the original problem, or reassessing outcomes.

nodes.name: Operational Translation
nodes.capability: Converts conceptual commitment into executable responsibilities, dependencies, and action conditions.
nodes.accepts: An adopted resolution and the operating context in which it must occur.
nodes.produces: An actionable configuration linking intent to concrete agency.
nodes.boundary: Specifies how the chosen mechanism becomes operable.
nodes.excludes: Selecting the resolution or evaluating its eventual effects.

nodes.name: Capability Mobilization
nodes.capability: Brings required agency, resources, access, and coordination into effective alignment.
nodes.accepts: Operational requirements, available capabilities, dependencies, and constraints.
nodes.produces: A functioning arrangement capable of performing the intervention.
nodes.boundary: Assembles and coordinates the means of realization.
nodes.excludes: Outcome valuation and post-action learning.

nodes.name: Intervention Performance
nodes.capability: Carries the selected mechanism through its relevant interactions with the problem situation.
nodes.accepts: An operational configuration, mobilized capabilities, and real conditions.
nodes.produces: Concrete state changes and observable effects.
nodes.boundary: Performs the intervention rather than merely planning or resourcing it.
nodes.excludes: Interpreting whether observed effects constitute success.

nodes.name: Resolution Regulation
nodes.capability: Keeps problem solving responsive by comparing unfolding reality with intent and revising the resolution system when warranted.
nodes.accepts: Success criteria, enacted changes, observations, deviations, and emerging conditions.
nodes.produces: Corrections, learning, escalation, or closure grounded in feedback.
nodes.boundary: Regulates the whole resolution across time without assuming the initial framing remains correct.
nodes.excludes: Treating execution completion alone as proof of resolution.

nodes.name: Outcome Sensing
nodes.capability: Detects relevant changes, side effects, and signals produced during and after intervention.
nodes.accepts: Observable conditions, success indicators, stakeholder experience, and anomaly signals.
nodes.produces: Timely evidence about outcomes and emerging conditions.
nodes.boundary: Acquires resolution-relevant feedback.
nodes.excludes: Explaining discrepancies or deciding revisions.

nodes.name: Discrepancy Interpretation
nodes.capability: Determines what differences between intended and observed outcomes imply about performance, models, criteria, or framing.
nodes.accepts: Outcome evidence, expectations, uncertainty, and success criteria.
nodes.produces: A localized account of why resolution is succeeding, failing, or becoming obsolete.
nodes.boundary: Diagnoses feedback at the level where revision is needed.
nodes.excludes: Executing the resulting revision.

nodes.name: Adaptive Revision
nodes.capability: Revises framing, understanding, design, commitment, or realization in response to interpreted feedback.
nodes.accepts: Diagnosed discrepancies, emerging opportunities, changed constraints, and retained learning.
nodes.produces: A corrected resolution state or a justified closure decision.
nodes.boundary: Routes learning back to the appropriate problem-solving dimension.
nodes.excludes: Assuming every discrepancy requires the same kind of correction.

edges.role: Constitute the problem that resolution must address.
edges.rationale: Problem solving cannot be coherent without distinguishing the relevant present condition, valued outcome, and governing boundary.

edges.role: Represent the relevant starting situation.
edges.rationale: A discrepancy cannot be resolved without an account of what currently obtains.

edges.role: Define what counts as satisfactory improvement.
edges.rationale: Change is not resolution unless some outcomes are valued over others.

edges.role: Bound what the problem includes and permits.
edges.rationale: Without a boundary, relevance, responsibility, and admissible change remain indeterminate.

edges.role: Explain persistence, dependency, and leverage within the constituted problem.
edges.rationale: Effective intervention requires some warranted understanding of how actions can affect outcomes.

edges.role: Calibrate the informational basis of understanding.
edges.rationale: An explanation must distinguish supported claims from gaps and unreliable appearances.

edges.role: Model the relationships that produce and transmit change.
edges.rationale: Evidence becomes actionable only when organized into mechanisms or functional dependencies.

edges.role: Preserve material uncertainty in the explanatory account.
edges.rationale: Every finite model has unknowns whose effects must remain visible to later design and judgment.

edges.role: Create coherent possible resolutions.
edges.rationale: Understanding a problem does not by itself supply the interventions capable of changing it.

edges.role: Generate distinct change mechanisms.
edges.rationale: Resolution synthesis requires a possibility space rather than an unexamined default.

edges.role: Anticipate each candidate's broader effects.
edges.rationale: Candidates cannot be meaningfully developed without considering how their effects propagate.

edges.role: Integrate intervention elements into coherent candidates.
edges.rationale: Individually plausible actions may conflict unless configured as a mutually supporting resolution.

edges.role: Adopt a defensible course of resolution.
edges.rationale: Possibilities cannot guide action until tradeoffs, uncertainty, and ownership yield commitment.

edges.role: Judge candidates across valued outcomes.
edges.rationale: Commitment must distinguish alternatives using the problem's plural criteria.

edges.role: Test candidates against uncertainty and failure.
edges.rationale: A nominally preferred option may be unacceptable when its fragility is considered.

edges.role: Convert judgment into owned adoption.
edges.rationale: Assessment alone does not create the authority or willingness required for action.

edges.role: Produce the intended change in reality.
edges.rationale: A selected resolution remains hypothetical until agency and means realize its mechanism.

edges.role: Translate resolution intent into operable action.
edges.rationale: Conceptual decisions require a faithful bridge to concrete responsibilities and dependencies.

edges.role: Align the capabilities required for enactment.
edges.rationale: An executable configuration cannot operate without sufficient agency, resources, access, and coordination.

edges.role: Perform the intervention in the problem situation.
edges.rationale: Preparation and mobilization produce no resolution unless the change mechanism is actually exercised.

edges.role: Regulate resolution through feedback and learning.
edges.rationale: Problem solving occurs in changing, partly known conditions and therefore requires correction or justified closure.

edges.role: Acquire evidence about unfolding outcomes.
edges.rationale: Regulation requires observations independent of prior expectations.

edges.role: Locate what observed discrepancies mean.
edges.rationale: Feedback cannot guide correction until deviations are attributed to performance, understanding, criteria, or framing.

edges.role: Revise the affected problem-solving dimensions.
edges.rationale: Interpreted learning must alter the relevant resolution state or support deliberate closure.

bootstrap.rationale: The bootstrap models Problem Solving as six mutually dependent outward capabilities: constituting what requires resolution, understanding how it behaves, synthesizing possible changes, committing under tradeoffs, realizing change, and regulating through feedback. Their children expose independent conceptual dimensions where another level materially improves routing. The carve is implementation-neutral and allows feedback to revise any earlier dimension.

summary: A first-principles bootstrap decomposes RootSolver into Problem Constitution, Explanatory Understanding, Resolution Synthesis, Resolution Commitment, Resolution Realization, and Resolution Regulation. Together they span the formation, direction, production, enactment, and correction of resolution without imposing a departmental workflow or domain taxonomy.
